title: Telling stories: yesterday and tomorrow
goal: String the short sentences you already have into a whole story — with linking words, aspect markers, plans, and the sentence-final particles that make you sound like a person, not a textbook.
bekal: tell events in order: 首先 · 跟住 · 之後 · 最後
add a twist with 點知 and an outcome with 結果
talk about plans with 會, 打算 and 諗住
wrap up a conversation like a Hong Konger

dialogs.title: 對話 1 — A weekend on Cheung Chau
dialogs.intro: Monday morning. Andi tells Mr. Chan about his Sunday. This is a full story in the past — and notice that not a single verb changes form.

lines.speaker: 陳生:
lines.text: [你星期日|Nei5 sing1 kei4 jat6][去咗邊度呀|heoi3 zo2 bin1 dou6 aa3]？
lines.id: Where did you go on Sunday?
lines.literal: you — week — day — go — already — which — place — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [去咗長洲|Heoi3 zo2 Coeng4 zau1]。[第一次去|Dai6 jat1 ci3 heoi3]，[好開心|hou2 hoi1 sam1]！
lines.id: Cheung Chau. It was my first time there — so much fun!
lines.literal: go — already — Cheung-Chau. order — one — time — go, filler — happy.

lines.speaker: 陳生:
lines.text: [講嚟聽下|Gong2 lei4 teng1 haa5]。[點去㗎|Dim2 heoi3 gaa3]？
lines.id: Tell me about it. How did you get there?
lines.literal: say — come — listen — a-bit. how — go — emphasis.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [首先|Sau2 sin1][我哋喺中環搭船|ngo5 dei6 hai2 Zung1 waan4 daap3 syun4]。[跟住|Gan1 zyu6][行咗成個朝早|haang4 zo2 seng4 go3 ziu1 zou2]。
lines.id: First we took the ferry from Central. Then we walked around all morning.
lines.literal: first — we — at — Central — take — boat. then — walk — already — whole — classifier — morning.

lines.speaker: 陳生:
lines.text: [食咗啲乜嘢呀|Sik6 zo2 di1 mat1 je5 aa3]？
lines.id: What did you eat?
lines.literal: eat — already — some — what — stuff — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [食咗好多海鮮|Sik6 zo2 hou2 do1 hoi2 sin1]。[之後|Zi1 hau6][我哋租咗單車|ngo5 dei6 zou1 zo2 daan1 ce1]。
lines.id: Loads of seafood. After that we rented bikes.
lines.literal: eat — already — filler — much — sea — fresh. after — we — rent — already — single — vehicle.

lines.speaker: 陳生:
lines.text: [你識踩單車咩|Nei5 sik1 caai2 daan1 ce1 me1]？
lines.id: Oh, you can ride a bike?
lines.literal: you — know-how — pedal — bicycle — really.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [識|Sik1]！[但係|Daan6 hai6][點知|dim2 zi1][踩咗十分鐘就落雨|caai2 zo2 sap6 fan1 zung1 zau6 lok6 jyu5]。
lines.id: I can! But guess what — ten minutes in, it started raining.
lines.literal: know-how. but — how — know — pedal — already — ten — minute — then — fall — rain.

lines.speaker: 陳生:
lines.text: [哈哈|Haa1 haa1]，[好慘|hou2 caam2]！[結果點呀|Git3 gwo2 dim2 aa3]？
lines.id: Haha, poor you! So what happened?
lines.literal: ha — ha, filler — miserable. result — how — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [結果|Git3 gwo2][我哋喺茶餐廳坐咗兩個鐘|ngo5 dei6 hai2 caa4 caan1 teng1 co5 zo2 loeng5 go3 zung1]。[好彩|Hou2 coi2][有奶茶飲|jau5 naai5 caa4 jam2]。
lines.id: We ended up sitting in a cha chaan teng for two hours. Luckily there was milk tea.
lines.literal: result — we — at — cha-chaan-teng — sit — already — two — classifier — hour. lucky — have — milk — tea — drink.

lines.speaker: 陳生:
lines.text: [咁最後呢|Gam2 zeoi3 hau6 ne1]？
lines.id: And in the end?
lines.literal: then — most — last — how.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [最後|Zeoi3 hau6][我哋濕晒返嚟|ngo5 dei6 sap1 saai3 faan1 lei4]。[但係|Daan6 hai6][我下次仲會去|ngo5 haa6 ci3 zung6 wui5 heoi3][㗎|gaa3]！
lines.id: In the end we came back soaked. But I'm still going again next time!
lines.literal: most — last — we — wet — completely — return — come. but — I — next — time — still — will — go — emphasis.

notes: **[講嚟聽下|Gong2 lei4 teng1 haa5] = “tell me about it”.** Literally “say come listen a bit”. A set phrase used to coax a story out of someone — learn it whole, don't take it apart.

**[首先|sau2 sin1] · [跟住|gan1 zyu6] · [之後|zi1 hau6] · [最後|zeoi3 hau6] are the four pillars of a story.** 🇭🇰 In everyday talk, [跟住|gan1 zyu6] is the most common — sometimes three or four times in one story, just like “and then” in English.

**⚠️ [點知|dim2 zi1] is one of the most Cantonese words there is.** Literally “how know”, it means “who'd have thought, and then guess what”. It marks an unexpected turn in a story, and almost no Hong Kong story goes without it. [點知佢冇嚟|Dim2 zi1 keoi5 mou5 lei4] = and then, turns out he didn't come.

**[結果|git3 gwo2] = in the end, as a result.** It goes in front of the sentence with the outcome. Its frequent partner: [本來|bun2 loi4] (originally). [本來想去，結果冇去|Bun2 loi4 soeng2 heoi3, git3 gwo2 mou5 heoi3] = I was going to go, but in the end I didn't.
**[好彩|hou2 coi2] = luckily, thank goodness.** Its opposite is [唔好彩|m4 hou2 coi2] = unlucky. [好彩你嚟咗|Hou2 coi2 nei5 lei4 zo2] = good thing you came.

**[有奶茶飲|jau5 naai5 caa4 jam2] = “there was milk tea to drink”.** ⚠️ Note the order: 有 + thing + verb. [有嘢食|jau5 je5 sik6] = there's food; [冇嘢做|mou5 je5 zou6] = nothing to do. The verb goes last, and this pattern is used a lot.

**[濕晒|sap1 saai3] = soaked through.** Remember 晒 from Unit 9 — it attaches to adjectives too, not just verbs: [食晒|sik6 saai3] (all eaten), [濕晒|sap1 saai3] (all wet), [攰晒|gui6 saai3] (completely worn out).

grammars.title: Stringing a story together
body: A Cantonese story is built from short sentences stitched together with linking words. You don't need long complex sentences — what you need is the right link between the short sentences you've already mastered.

head: Whole story
Meaning
rows: [本來我打算返工|Bun2 loi4 ngo5 daa2 syun3 faan1 gung1]，
I was planning to go to work,
[點知琴晚發燒|dim2 zi1 kam4 maan5 faat3 siu1]，
but then I got a fever last night,
[結果請咗假|git3 gwo2 cing2 zo2 gaa3]。
so I ended up taking the day off.
[好彩老闆冇嬲|Hou2 coi2 lou5 baan2 mou5 nau1]。

after: **The time words from Unit 5 still apply inside each sentence.** The linker comes first, then the time, then the subject, then the rest: [跟住琴日我去咗旺角|Gan1 zyu6 kam4 jat6 ngo5 heoi3 zo2 Wong6 gok3]。
🇭🇰 **Don't be afraid to repeat [跟住|gan1 zyu6].** In spoken Hong Kong stories, using it three times in a row is completely normal and actually sounds natural.

dialogs.title: 對話 2 — Plans for next year
dialogs.intro: The closing conversation of this module. Wong Lai and Andi talk about plans — and almost every pattern you've learned in twelve units shows up here at least once.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [你聖誕節|Nei5 sing3 daan3 zit3][打算做咩呀|daa2 syun3 zou6 me1 aa3]？
lines.id: What are you planning to do for Christmas?
lines.literal: you — holy — birth — festival — plan — do — what — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [我諗住返印尼|Ngo5 nam2 zyu6 faan1 Jan3 nei4]。[一年冇返過屋企喇|Jat1 nin4 mou5 faan1 gwo3 uk1 kei2 laa3]。
lines.id: I'm thinking of going back to Indonesia. I haven't been home for a year.
lines.literal: I — think — keep — return — Indonesia. one — year — not — return — ever — home — already.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [你幾時走呀|Nei5 gei2 si4 zau2 aa3]？[買咗機票未|Maai5 zo2 gei1 piu3 mei6]？
lines.id: When are you leaving? Have you bought a ticket yet?
lines.literal: you — what — time — go — huh. buy — already — plane — ticket — not-yet.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [仲未|Zung6 mei6]，[太貴喇|taai3 gwai3 laa3]。[我等緊平啲嘅|Ngo5 dang2 gan2 peng4 di1 ge3]。
lines.id: Not yet, they're way too expensive. I'm waiting for a cheaper one.
lines.literal: still — not-yet, too — expensive — already. I — wait — -ing — cheap — a-bit — possessive.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [愈遲買愈貴㗎|Jyu6 ci4 maai5 jyu6 gwai3 gaa3]！[快啲買啦|Faai3 di1 maai5 laa1]。
lines.id: The later you buy, the pricier it gets! Hurry up and buy one.
lines.literal: the-more — late — buy — the-more — expensive — emphasis. fast — a-bit — buy — go-on.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [我知喇|Ngo5 zi1 laa3]。[今晚一定買|Gam1 maan5 jat1 ding6 maai5]。[你呢|Nei5 ne1]？[你會唔會去旅行呀|Nei5 wui5 m4 wui5 heoi3 leoi5 hang4 aa3]？
lines.id: OK, OK. I'll definitely buy one tonight. And you? Going on a trip?
lines.literal: I — know — already. this — night — surely — buy. you — how. you — will — not — will — go — travel — huh.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [想|Soeng2]，[但係要儲錢|daan6 hai6 jiu3 cou5 cin2]。[我打算出年去日本|Ngo5 daa2 syun3 ceot1 nin2 heoi3 Jat6 bun2]。
lines.id: I'd like to, but I need to save up. I'm planning to go to Japan next year.
lines.literal: want, but — need — store — money. I — plan — next — year — go — Japan.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [好呀|Hou2 aa3]！[我未去過日本|Ngo5 mei6 heoi3 gwo3 Jat6 bun2]。[不如一齊去|Bat1 jyu4 jat1 cai4 heoi3][好唔好|hou2 m4 hou2]？
lines.id: Great! I've never been to Japan. How about we go together?
lines.literal: good — huh. I — not-yet — go — ever — Japan. how-about — together — go — good — not — good.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [得呀|Dak1 aa3]！[但係你要學多啲日文|Daan6 hai6 nei5 jiu3 hok6 do1 di1 Jat6 man2][喎|wo3]。
lines.id: Sure! But you'll have to study more Japanese, you know.
lines.literal: can — huh. but — you — must — learn — more — a-bit — Japanese — writing — you-know.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [唉|Aai1]，[我廣東話都仲未學好|ngo5 Gwong2 dung1 waa2 dou1 zung6 mei6 hok6 hou2][添|tim1]！
lines.id: Oh no, I haven't even got my Cantonese right yet!
lines.literal: oh-no, I — Cantonese — speech — even — still — not-yet — learn — well — on-top.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [你講得好好㗎喇|Nei5 gong2 dak1 hou2 hou2 gaa3 laa3]！[一年前你乜都唔識|Jat1 nin4 cin4 nei5 mat1 dou1 m4 sik1]，[而家傾成個鐘都得|ji4 gaa1 king1 seng4 go3 zung1 dou1 dak1]。
lines.id: You already speak really well! A year ago you couldn't say anything, now you can chat for a whole hour.
lines.literal: you — speak — manner — filler — good — emphasis — already. one — year — before — you — what — all — not — know-how, now — chat — whole — classifier — hour — also — can.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [多謝晒|Do1 ze6 saai3]。[都係因為有你教我|Dou1 hai6 jan1 wai6 jau5 nei5 gaau3 ngo5]。[加油|Gaa1 jau2]，[我哋一齊努力|ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 nou5 lik6]！
lines.id: Thank you so much. It's all because you taught me. Let's keep at it together!
lines.literal: thank — completely. all — is — because — have — you — teach — me. add — oil, we — together — strive — effort.

notes: **Three ways to talk about plans, from the loosest to the most certain:** [想|soeng2] (want — Unit 4), [諗住|nam2 zyu6] (thinking of, intend), [打算|daa2 syun3] (plan, thought it through), [會|wui5] (will — definitely happening).
**[愈…愈…|jyu6 … jyu6 …] = the more … the more ….** The form you saw in Unit 11 as 越…越…; both characters are in use. [愈嚟愈好|jyu6 lei4 jyu6 hou2] = better and better.
**[出年|ceot1 nin2] = next year.** 🇭🇰 A native Cantonese form; not 明年 as in Mandarin. [舊年|gau6 nin2] = last year; [今年|gam1 nin2] = this year.

**[講得好好|gong2 dak1 hou2 hou2] = “speaks really well”.** The pattern verb + [得|dak1] + adjective describes **how** an action is done. [行得好快|haang4 dak1 hou2 faai3] (walks fast), [食得好慢|sik6 dak1 hou2 maan6] (eats slowly). ⚠️ This is a different 得 from 得 “can” in Unit 10 — what follows tells them apart.

**[添|tim1] at the end of a sentence = “on top of that, too”.** It adds something that makes things worse or more. [唔夠錢，仲遲到添|M4 gau3 cin2, zung6 ci4 dou3 tim1] = not enough money, and late on top of that.
**[傾|king1] = to chat.** [傾偈|king1 gai2] = to have a long chat. A native Cantonese word used constantly; Mandarin uses 聊天.

**[加油|gaa1 jau2] = come on, you can do it!** Literally “add oil”. Said to someone who's working hard at something — an exam, a job, practice. 🇭🇰 In Cantonese it's *gaa1 jau2*, not *jiāyóu* as in Mandarin.

grammars.title: Sentence-final particles: a summary
body: This is what the introduction promised. Particles don't change what your sentence means — they change how it **feels**, and without them your grammatically correct sentences sound like a machine. Master the first six; the rest will come from listening.

head: Particle
Adds
Example
rows: [佢係老師㗎|Keoi5 hai6 lou5 si1 gaa3]。 She really is a teacher.
[落雨喎|Lok6 jyu5 wo3]。 Oh, it's raining.
[你唔去咩|Nei5 m4 heoi3 me1]？ What, you're not going?
[十蚊啫|Sap6 man1 ze1]。 It's only ten dollars.
[得一個咋|Dak1 jat1 go3 zaa3]。 There's only one.
[咁咪去囉|Gam2 mai6 heoi3 lo1]。 Just go, then.
[仲遲到添|Zung6 ci4 dou3 tim1]。 And late, too.
[佢好好人嘅|Keoi5 hou2 hou2 jan4 ge3]。 He's a genuinely nice person.
[我講咗吖嘛|Ngo5 gong2 zo2 aa1 maa3]。 See, I told you.

after: ⚠️ **Particles can't be stacked at random, but some do come in pairs**: [㗎喇|gaa3 laa3] (that's how it is now), [㗎嘛|gaa3 maa3] (well, that's just how it is), [啦嘛|laa1 maa3]. Learn these pairs by listening, not by building them yourself.

**A sentence without a particle isn't wrong — it's just flat.** Formal writing does drop them. But in conversation, a sentence without a particle sounds cold or rushed, and that's not the impression you want.
🇭🇰 **The fastest way to master them: copy one particle a week.** Pick 呀, use it in all your questions for a week, then move on to 啦. Memorizing this whole table at once has never worked for anyone.

head: Form
Meaning
Example
rows: [我想去日本|Ngo5 soeng2 heoi3 Jat6 bun2]。
[我諗住返屋企|Ngo5 nam2 zyu6 faan1 uk1 kei2]。
[我打算出年去|Ngo5 daa2 syun3 ceot1 nin2 heoi3]。
[我一定會嚟|Ngo5 jat1 ding6 wui5 lei4]。
[我唔會遲到|Ngo5 m4 wui5 ci4 dou3]。
[希望快啲好返|Hei1 mong6 faai3 di1 hou2 faan1]。

blocks.title: Hong Kong holidays you should know
items: [農曆新年|Nung4 lik6 san1 nin4] Lunar New Year — the longest holiday. The greetings are [恭喜發財|Gung1 hei2 faat3 coi4]！ and [新年快樂|San1 nin4 faai3 lok6]！
[中秋節|Zung1 cau1 zit3] Mid-Autumn Festival — mooncakes and lanterns.
[端午節|Dyun1 ng5 zit3] Dragon Boat Festival — rice dumplings and boat races.
[聖誕節|Sing3 daan3 zit3] Christmas — [聖誕快樂|Sing3 daan3 faai3 lok6]！
[生日快樂|Saang1 jat6 faai3 lok6]！ Happy birthday. [恭喜晒|Gung1 hei2 saai3]！ Congratulations (for any good news).

sections.title: Wrapping up a conversation, and what you have now

blocks.text: Twelve units ago, you couldn't say a single sentence. This page is the final check: if you can do everything on the list below, you have real A1 Cantonese.

head: Wrapping up
Meaning
rows: [有咩事call我|Jau5 me1 si6 call ngo5]。
Call me if anything comes up.

items: Introduce yourself: name, surname, where you're from, your job — and ask back. *(Unit 1)*
Talk about family, age, quantities and phone numbers with the right classifiers. *(Unit 2)*
Ask prices, say amounts of money, and haggle without sounding rude. *(Unit 3)*
Order at a cha chaan teng and at yum cha, complete with 走甜 and 埋單. *(Unit 4)*
Tell the time with 個字, say days and dates, make appointments. *(Unit 5)*
Ask for directions, understand the answer, and ride every kind of Hong Kong transport. *(Unit 6)*
Put 喺 in the right place and describe where you live. *(Unit 7)*
Use adjectives without 係 and compare with 過, 冇咁, 最. *(Unit 8)*
Use 咗, 緊, 過 — and negate them with 冇 or 未, not 唔. *(Unit 9)*
Make calls, ask for favors, say no politely, reschedule. *(Unit 10)*
Describe symptoms, talk to a doctor, give advice and prohibitions. *(Unit 11)*
Tell what happened yesterday and what's planned for tomorrow, with a particle at the end. *(Unit 12)*

blocks.title: Three things that matter most from here
items: **Find one person to talk to every week.** Not a teacher, not an app — one real person. Forty minutes a week with someone who waits for you to finish your sentence beats anything else.
**Copy one particle a week.** Your grammar is already good enough to be understood; particles are what make you sound like a person.

**Don't stop out of fear of getting the tones wrong.** Hong Kongers are used to hearing Cantonese with tones that slip, and they still understand from the rest of the sentence. What stops them understanding isn't your wrong tone, but the sentence you never said.

blocks.text: 多謝晒你讀完呢本書。加油 — *do1 ze6 saai3 nei5 duk6 jyun4 ni1 bun2 syu1. Gaa1 jau2.* Thank you for finishing this module. Keep going.

items: [好|Hou2] ___。 (agreeing in a friendly way)

answers: 首先 — 跟住 — 點知 — 結果 — 好彩
打算 — 想 — 唔會 — 會 — 會
